title: Compact executive alignment brief + facilitator cues
content:
Purpose:
A short, facilitator-friendly QBR runbook designed for executive-level alignment. Use when the customer prefers a concise, decision-driven meeting (35–50 minutes). This doc combines: a tight agenda, spoken facilitator cues, preflight checklist, renewal / upsell signals table, and explicit next-step templates.

Audience:
- CS lead (owner)
- Customer executive sponsors
- Product or solutions engineer (optional for demo+roadmap questions)

Timebox and flow (45 minutes recommended):
- 0:00–0:05 — Quick hello & landing (facilitator)
  - Cues: "Thanks everyone for joining. We'll keep this to 45 minutes and surface three areas for decisions by the end."
- 0:05–0:12 — Health snapshot (customer metrics + signal highlights)
  - Slide: 1-pager health card (usage, latency, errors, adoption signals)
  - Cues: "Topline: platform availability was X, key usage trends are Y, the risk signal to watch is Z."
- 0:12–0:22 — Business impact stories (customer testimony / recent wins)
  - Cues: "Quick customer quote or internal case: two bullets — what changed and customer outcome."
- 0:22–0:32 — Roadmap & alignment (product changes, upcoming features, compatibility)
  - Cues: "Here are three items we recommend you evaluate for next quarter and how each affects cost/perf."
- 0:32–0:42 — Renewal / commercial discussion & decision framing
  - Cues: "We want to confirm two asks: renewal posture (yes/needs follow up) and priority for next-quarter investment."
- 0:42–0:45 — Decisions recap and owners
  - Cues: "Recap decisions, owners, dates. I'll follow up with a summary and calendar invites."

Pre-meeting 'preflight' checklist (owner: CS lead) — complete 48h prior:
- Share short agenda with customer sponsor + confirm 45-minute slot
- Send 1-slide health snapshot draft for customer to validate
- Run internal sync w/ solutions engineer if demo or deep product Qs expected
- Confirm point person (customer) for procurement/renewal conversation
- Confirm recording permissions and notetaker

Facilitator script snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- Opening: "Appreciate your time — goal is alignment and a clear set of actions by EOD."
- Health intro: "Three numbers to know: availability, top 3 customers by usage, and any exec-flag incidents."
- Transition to roadmap: "Based on your usage profile, we see 3 roadmap items that map to your priorities; we want to make sure we sequence them correctly."
- Renewal ask: "Given the value we've delivered and upcoming priorities, what's the preferred cadence for renewal conversations? Are we looking for a 'green' go-ahead or do you want a follow-up week?"
- Close: "Thanks — I'll circulate the note with owners and proposed dates for follow-ups."

Decision log (one-line per decision) — capture during meeting:
- Decision: <short phrase> | Owner: <name> | Due: <YYYY-MM-DD> | Confidence: high/medium/low

Renewal & risk signals (quick reference):
- Green (likely to renew): steady or increasing usage, executive sponsor present, contract discussions started
- Yellow (needs nurturing): flat usage, 1 minor incident, procurement readiness unclear
- Red (at risk): declining usage >20% QoQ, major unremediated incident, competing vendor evaluation underway

Commercial prompt language (templates):
- If green: "Based on current trajectory, we recommend moving to a 12-month renewal with reserved capacity X to reduce per-token costs by Y%. Would you like a formal proposal?"
- If yellow: "We can explore a short-term bridge (3–6 months) with checkpoints to validate impact; shall we set cadence?"
- If red: "We hear concerns on X. Can we schedule a follow-up with product to address the technical gap and propose mitigations in 7 days?"

Post-meeting follow-up (within 24h):
- Send meeting note with decisions table and action owners
- Attach validated health snapshot + suggested commercial proposal (if applicable)
- Book follow-up technical deep-dive (if requested) and loop in AE/procurement

Appendix A — Health snapshot fields (single-slide format):
- Topline: active seats / API calls / avg tokens per request
- Reliability: SLA uptime last 90 days, P99 latency, critical errors count
- Adoption: features used (ranked), internal champions, reference projects
- Spend: monthly committed vs actual, cost per token trend

Appendix B — Facilitation notes (things we often forget):
- Re-ask the customer's objective at the top of the call to keep the meeting outcome-driven
- Keep slides to a single visual point per slide (exec-friendly)
- Avoid showing raw logs or long error traces; surface remediation status instead
- Call out decisions visibly on slide 2 so execs can confirm quickly

Notes to self / open questions:
- Consider a one-click deck template we can reuse across accounts (product/metrics placeholders)
- Add a short rubric for confidence scoring of renewal signal (quantify thresholds)
- Follow up with marketing for a concise customer success one-pager to attach to green renewals

Version history:
- Draft 0.1 — initial outline (2025-10-02) — Priya
- Draft 0.5 — added decision templates & risk signals (2025-11-15) — Marcus
- Draft 1.0 — validated with AE playbook (2026-01-12) — Ana

Linked artifacts and quick refs:
- Confluence QBR playbook (link above)
- Slack: #cs-qbr-prep (for last-minute coordination)
- Template proposal: sales/proposals/template-v2.docx

-----
If this doc is used as the canonical exec brief, keep it short, move detail to the follow-up packet, and always end with 2 explicit asks for the sponsor (one tactical, one strategic).
